trajectory_summary: The call opens with a legitimate technical concern and heavy accessibility friction (hearing, low-tech, third-party assistance needed), but the rep stays patient throughout, successfully secures the usage data via a workaround, and books a next-day appointment with a specific time. Energy builds steadily from guarded-and-confused to warm-and-committed, aided by an extended personal rapport tangent about bicycle racing that the customer initiated and sustained.
outcome_dispute: v1 tag is unknown/unclear; observed transcript shows a clear booked outcome — day (tomorrow, the 20th) and time (10AM) were both confirmed with a customer-side calendar check, so this should be tagged booked, not tentative or callback.

observed_outcome.quote: Okay. Everything's clear on the twentieth. I'll see you tomorrow or somewhere tomorrow.
observed_outcome.reasoning: A specific day (tomorrow, the 20th) and time (10AM) were confirmed with the customer actively checking his own calendar, meeting the booked bar. The wife/co-owner identified earlier was never brought into the appointment confirmation, so co_owner_confirmed is false.

bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: A usage-pattern observation (higher winter draw) surfaces directly from the customer's household while pulling up the bill graph, but the rep does not respond to or use this line at all — no flip into emotional alignment against the utility or into curiosity about the design occurred.

You care for the environment' but never references this environmental motivation again later in the call, including at booking.

primary_coaching_focus.quote: We got you down. We'll see you tomorrow at at 10AM. Okay? 10AM.
primary_coaching_focus.why: Despite locking a real day and time, the rep skipped nearly every required button-up element — no hour-block framing, no no-driving/computer instruction, no verbal 'is that fair?' handshake, no text-confirmation promise. Schema ties these directly to no-show rate, and this customer's hearing/tech difficulties make a written confirmation especially important; this is the single highest-leverage fix for protecting an appointment that was hard-won.

key_moments.quote: Honestly, your roof your roof is fine. And how it is, it's totally fine.
key_moments.stewart_read: Rep gives a confident technical assessment of roof suitability (east-west orientation) without deferring to the specialist, which is setter-scope content delivered as fact rather than routed. It calmed the customer effectively, but the rep is not qualified to make that call.

key_moments.quote: Anybody else on the title but you? My wife, Anne.
key_moments.stewart_read: A co-owner (wife, Anne) is explicitly identified on the title, which per protocol requires inclusion in the appointment. The rep acknowledges with a bare 'K.' and never returns to this at booking.

key_moments.quote: Okay. I could do 1 to 200 for now.
key_moments.stewart_read: Rep fills a placeholder bill range when the customer can't produce a number, then moves on without ever circling back to get a real figure or using it as emotional leverage. The more supported read is strategic-procedural: this looks like a CRM required-field workaround (a range within 'the safe zone') rather than an attempt to fabricate pitch material, since the rep never references this number again to build a case.

key_moments.quote: I I used to race bicycles.
key_moments.stewart_read: Not a solar-specific enthusiasm signal (no EV, pool, or usage-driver), but it is a genuine rapport-building moment the customer initiated and sustained for several minutes while waiting on his son — this kept the customer engaged during dead time rather than losing him to frustration.
